title: Level 5 (World Class) - A-23
notes:
West leads the ♦K against 3NT. The defense starts with 4 rounds of diamonds and switches to clubs. South pitched 2 clubs on the diamonds because West is marked with the ♥K by his opening bid.

A second round of clubs is cashed on which West discards. If South now cashes a top spade in dummy and crosses to the ♠A, East's ability to follow to both rounds will reveal a complete count of the hand (West must be 5431). If West has the ♥9 the contract can no longer be made.

If South cashes the ♣Q, West will discard his remaining spade and dummy will be one suit squeezed in hearts. If the ♥8 is discarded South will be able to take only one heart finesse as the suit will be blocked.

If the ♥Q or ♥J is discarded West will be able to cover the ♥10 with the ♥K and take a trick with the ♥9. Refusing to cash the ♣Q is no better. As before, West can cover the ♥10 with the ♥K and take a trick at the end with the ♥9.

South can make the contract with the help of an entry squeeze. An entry squeeze is an ending that does not directly produce an extra trick, just an extra entry. The entry gained can be used, for example, to counter the threat of a one suit squeeze.

After cashing 1 round of spades, dummy's remaining spade honour should be played and overtaken with the ♠A. The ♣Q will now squeeze West instead of North. If West throws a heart, the spade loser that was just created is thrown from dummy. 4 heart tricks can now be taken by leading the ♥10 on the first round.

If West throws his last spade on the ♣Q the ♥8 is discarded from dummy. South can take one heart finesse immediately. The South hand now contains another spade entry to take a second heart finesse.
